snapshot.title: Time Jump — 12:00 PM — Firmware Patch Confirmed

fields.narration: Facilitator → All: It is now 12:00 PM. The Systems & Cybersecurity Lead has confirmed that firmware patch v2.3.2 has been tested in the sandbox environment and successfully restores proper failover logic. The patch has been signed by the Chief Remote Pilot and the ASO. The root cause — a corrupted failover logic in firmware 2.4.11a — has been confirmed. The ASO has determined that no further NTSB reporting is required beyond the initial submission, as the event is now fully documented.
worldState: The firmware patch v2.3.2 has been successfully tested in the sandbox environment.
The patch has been signed by the Chief Remote Pilot (CRP) and the Aviation Safety Officer (ASO).
The root cause of the link loss and unauthorized airspace penetration — a corrupted failover logic in firmware 2.4.11a — has been confirmed and documented.
The ASO has closed the NTSB reporting loop; no further submissions are required.
The hazard log (HUOG-ISP Section 11.1) has been updated with the final root cause and mitigation plan.
The fleet remains grounded pending final approval for a return to flight under degraded conditions.
fields.facilitatorNote: This time jump confirms the root cause is resolved and the patch is approved. The ASO must now finalize the hazard log entry. Players should now begin the return-to-flight planning under HUOG-FOM 4.3 and HUOG-ERP Section 11.1.
